Blood cells, surface proteins and plasma measurements of patients with COVID-19 from the INCOV cohort

Source: R/data-docs.R
incov_pbmc_subset.Rd

A SingleCellExposomeExperiment with the raw counts of 1,032 blood mononuclear cells from 43 patients of the INCOV cohort (Su et al. 2020) at their first blood draw: 14 monocytes and 10 T cells per patient, with the counts of 192 antibodies for the same cells, four of them isotype controls, 13 plasma compounds of exogenous origin among the donor variables and 182 plasma metabolites of the same draw. It is a small real data set for the functions that need more than transcript counts: surface proteins, exposure measurements with missing values, and a second omic layer measured once per donor. It shows how these functions are used on real data. With at most 14 cells per donor and cell type it is far too small to support conclusions, and all its donors had an acute viral infection.

Format

An RDS file, inst/extdata/incov_pbmc_subset.rds, read with readRDS(system.file("extdata", "incov_pbmc_subset.rds", package = "exposomeSC")).

Source

The clinical records and the plasma measurements are Table S1 of Mendeley Data, doi:10.17632/tzydswhhb5.5 (version 5, published on 4 November 2020), distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence (CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The plasma values were selected, not changed; smoking and sex were recoded as described above.

The single-cell values of genes and surface proteins are from ArrayExpress accession E-MTAB-9357 (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/arrayexpress/studies/E-MTAB-9357), released on 29 October 2020 and downloaded on 19 November 2026. On 21 November 2026 the authors who deposited the accession gave permission in these words: "The single-cell values from E-MTAB-9357 included in exposomeSC may be used and redistributed under CC BY 4.0, with citation of Su et al. (2020)." The object holds a subset of the values that the authors released, transformed as described above.

The object as a whole is therefore distributed under CC BY 4.0. Work that uses it should cite Su et al. (2020). The permission does not imply that the authors endorse exposomeSC.

The article itself is published under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. The values in this object come from the data that the authors deposited in Mendeley Data and ArrayExpress, not from the article.

The object was made by inst/scripts/make_incov_pbmc_subset.R, which checks the size and the SHA-256 of every input file and carries out the steps described above.

Details

Donors

Patients of the INCOV cohort who, at their first blood draw, had single cells, plasma metabolomics and plasma proteomics measured, a recorded history of cigarette smoking, and were not in hospital (WHO ordinal scale 1 or 2). 43 patients meet these conditions: 37 women and 6 men aged 19 to 81, 16 of them current or former smokers. The rule was fixed from the clinical sheet and the list of files before any single-cell value of these donors was read.

Counts

assay(x, "counts"): 15,406 genes by 1,032 cells, as a sparse matrix; the rows are gene symbols. The archive holds the natural logarithm of one plus the counts per million of each cell, from which the counts were recovered: every value of a cell is a whole multiple of the value of one count, and that value times the total of the cell is one million, which the script checks for every cell. Genes without a count in these cells are left out, so the column sums are those of all 24,966 genes of the archive files. The authors had kept cells with at least 200 genes, fewer than 10,000 counts, fewer than 2,500 genes and under 10 per cent mitochondrial counts.

Surface proteins

altExp(x, "CITE"): the counts of 192 antibodies, four of them isotype controls, for the same cells, recovered in the same way.

Cell types

x$cell_type, assigned for this data set; the archive holds no cell types. Each sample has two gates, one for the protein CD3 and one for the sum of the proteins CD14, CD11c, CD33 and CD64. A gate is the midpoint of the two centres that a split of the cells into two groups by the logarithm of one plus the count gives. A "T cell" has CD3 above its gate, the sum not above its gate, and fewer than 10 counts of the genes LYZ, S100A8 and S100A9 together. A "Monocyte" has the sum above its gate, CD3 not above its gate, at least 5 counts of those three genes and fewer than 3 counts of CD3D, CD3E and TRAC together. Of the 63,865 cells of the 43 samples, 9,889 are monocytes and 38,213 T cells by this rule. In one sample, INCOV132, the two groups of the sum lie close together (its gate is 8.8 counts, the lowest; the others are 12 or more): 121 of its 328 cells lie above both gates and are neither kind, against fewer than a tenth of the cells of any other sample, and of the 43 cells that the gates alone would make monocytes the conditions on the genes keep 16. The rule was chosen by how well alternatives agreed with these genes in 42 of the samples and was applied to the 43rd as it stood. The five proteins and six genes of the rule are constrained by it and must not be read as results.

Cells

14 monocytes and 10 T cells per donor, drawn at random with a fixed seed from the cells of each kind. The two numbers were set by the size limit of a Bioconductor source package.

Cell annotations

colData(x): donor_id (the patient identifier of the study), cell_type, sample_id (the name of the sample in the archive, the patient identifier followed by -BL) and archive_cell (the name of the cell in the files of the archive). The column names of the object are the patient identifier and the barcode of the cell. The rows are named by gene symbol, which rowData(x)$symbol repeats.

Donor variables

exposureData(x), one row per donor: ever_smoker (1 = current or former smoker, 0 = never smoker), age (years), sex_male (1 = male, 0 = female), and the plasma levels of 13 compounds of exogenous origin: cotinine; caffeine, paraxanthine and theobromine; pfos and pfoa (perfluorooctanesulfonate and perfluorooctanoate); methylparaben_sulfate and propylparaben_sulfate; hydroxychlorothalonil; naphthol_sulfate; ethyl_glucuronide; saccharin and acesulfame. The levels are relative abundances, scaled by the authors so that the median of a compound within a batch is 1, and NA where the table has no value for the sample. Ten of the 13 compounds lack a value for at least one donor: cotinine has a value for only 5 donors, propylparaben sulfate for 17, acesulfame for 19 and saccharin for 27. The table does not say why a value is missing. In measurements of this kind the usual reason is that the compound was not detected in the sample, but it is not the only one: the table also lacks a value of glucose for one of these donors. exposureInfo(x) gives the name of each compound in the source table (source_name), its family, and lowest_reported, the smallest value of the compound among the 387 samples of the table. The table reports no limits of detection. For the metabolites that they analysed, those with fewer than 20 per cent of the values missing, the authors put this smallest value in place of a missing one; six of the 13 compounds here have more missing values than that. The 13 compounds were chosen by their kind, from their names and the numbers of samples with a value.

Plasma metabolites

metadata(x)$plasma_metabolites, 43 donors by 182 metabolites: the metabolites that the source table assigns to a super-pathway other than xenobiotics and reports for all 43 donors, on the same relative scale. Their pathways are in metadata(x)$metabolite_info.

Provenance

metadata(x)$source: the reference, the sources and their licences, the permission for the single-cell values (single_cells$permission), the names, sizes and SHA-256 of the 88 input files, the selection rule, the gates of each sample (gates) and the numbers of monocytes, T cells and other cells of each donor (gated_cells).

The rule for the donors, the rule for the cell types, the numbers of cells and the seed were fixed before any association of a donor variable with expression, proteins or metabolites was computed on these donors. The object was first made from 42 of the 43 donors, because the first transfer of the expression file of one was incomplete, and the vignettes were first written on that version. It was then made again from all 43 by the script without that exclusion; the cells of the 14 donors that follow that donor in the order of the draw are a new random draw.

References

Su Y, Chen D, Yuan D, et al. (2020). Multi-omics resolves a sharp disease-state shift between mild and moderate COVID-19. Cell, 183(6), 1479-1495.e20. doi:10.1016/j.cell.2020.10.037

Examples

x <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "incov_pbmc_subset.rds",
    package = "exposomeSC"))
x
#> class: SingleCellExposomeExperiment 
#> dim: 15406 1032 
#> metadata(3): source plasma_metabolites metabolite_info
#> assays(1): counts
#> rownames(15406): A1BG A1BG-AS1 ... ZYX ZZEF1
#> rowData names(1): symbol
#> colnames(1032): INCOV039_AAGACCTAGGGTCTCC INCOV039_ACTGTCCGTGAGGCTA ...
#>   INCOV135_GGCGTGTGTACCGTAT INCOV135_GTATCTTAGAAACGCC
#> colData names(4): donor_id cell_type sample_id archive_cell
#> reducedDimNames(0):
#> mainExpName: NULL
#> altExpNames(1): CITE
#> exposureData(43 samples x 16 exposures): ever_smoker, age, sex_male, cotinine, caffeine ...
#> sampleColumn: donor_id
table(x$cell_type)
#> 
#> Monocyte   T cell 
#>      602      430 
exposureData(x)[1:3, 1:6]
#>          ever_smoker age sex_male cotinine  caffeine paraxanthine
#> INCOV039           0  38        0       NA 9.8244059           NA
#> INCOV042           0  60        0       NA 0.9791921    0.3850829
#> INCOV056           1  61        0       NA 6.3010545    2.1963925
SingleCellExperiment::altExp(x, "CITE")
#> class: SummarizedExperiment 
#> dim: 192 1032 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(1): counts
#> rownames(192): B7-H4 CD10 ... XCR1-1 c-Met
#> rowData names(0):
#> colnames(1032): INCOV039_AAGACCTAGGGTCTCC INCOV039_ACTGTCCGTGAGGCTA ...
#>   INCOV135_GGCGTGTGTACCGTAT INCOV135_GTATCTTAGAAACGCC
#> colData names(0):
dim(S4Vectors::metadata(x)$plasma_metabolites)
#> [1]  43 182
S4Vectors::metadata(x)$source$single_cells$licence
#> [1] "CC BY 4.0"
